title: Page 1
summary: A July 18, 1969 memo drafted by Bill Safire for H. R. Haldeman, to be used in the event of a Moon disaster. It states that Apollo astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin Aldrin would die on the Moon, framing their sacrifice as serving humanity's search for truth. It describes their families, nation, world, and Earth mourning them, says their exploration united the world and strengthened human brotherhood, and compares them to ancient star-constellation heroes.

title: Page 2
summary: A closing passage addressed to the mission's crew and the nation: the first men to reach the moon will be remembered, and future moon-gazers will know part of another world belongs to mankind. Before the President's statement, the President should phone each widow-to-be. After NASA ends communications with the men, a clergyman should commend their souls to the deep in a burial-at-sea style, ending with the Lord's Prayer.
